conventions: Include the standard Backstage Apache-2.0 license header at the top of every TypeScript/TSX file.
Use TypeScript strict typing matching existing @backstage/frontend-app-api and @backstage/frontend-plugin-api conventions.
Format all files according to @backstage/cli/config/prettier (single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indentation).

Use const instead of let for any variable that is only assigned once (including variables captured by nested closures that are assigned once before the closure is invoked) to satisfy ESLint prefer-const.
Do not run ESLint with --fix and do not hand-edit report*.api.md files; regenerate API reports via yarn build:api-reports.
Use Jest and @testing-library/react for unit and integration tests.

decisions.topic: Unregistered ancestor route ref handling in RouteResolver
decisions.choice: Return undefined from resolveBasePath and RouteResolver.resolve when any ancestor RouteRef in refDiffList has no entry in routePaths
rejected: Throw Error('No path for ...') when an ancestor RouteRef is missing from routePaths
Skip missing ancestor segments and resolve a partial path
decisions.reason: During bootstrap only a partial tree is instantiated so ancestor route paths may not be registered yet, and useRouteRef is documented to return undefined when a route cannot be resolved.

decisions.choice: Add optional subscribe?(listener: () => void): () => void method to RouteResolutionApi and implement it on RouteResolutionApiProxy to notify listeners whenever initialize() updates the delegate RouteResolver
rejected: Replace RouteResolutionApiProxy instance identity in ApiHolder after finalization
decisions.reason: An optional subscribe method preserves backward compatibility for custom implementations and test mocks while allowing in-place re-initialization of RouteResolutionApiProxy to notify mounted hooks.

decisions.choice: Subscribe to routeResolutionApi.subscribe?.() in useEffect to increment a local state counter included in useMemo dependencies, and immediately re-check routeResolutionApi.resolve inside useEffect when the preceding render resolved to undefined so finalization occurring between initial render and effect subscription is also caught
rejected: Only wait for future subscribe listener notifications without checking in useEffect whether finalization already happened between initial render and subscription
Use useSyncExternalStore directly with routeResolutionApi.resolve as getSnapshot
Call routeResolutionApi.resolve on every render without memoization
decisions.reason: Re-checking in useEffect right after subscribing closes the window where initialize() runs between the first render and effect commit, while avoiding infinite render loops from new closure instances returned by RouteResolver.resolve.

sites.first_line: We use the `useRouteRef` hook to create a link generator function that returns the details page path. First we need to check whether the route is available, the link generator function will be `undefined` if it isn't. The route can be unavailable if it, or any of its ancestor routes, has not been registered yet. This can happen during app startup, for example in app root elements that are rendered before route resolution has been finalized. In that case `useRouteRef` returns `undefined` at first, and the component automatically re-renders with the resolved link generator once the app has been finalized. We then call the link generator, passing it an object with the kind, namespace, and name. These parameters are used to construct a concrete path to the "Foo" details page.
sites.rule: Keep the explanation that useRouteRef returns undefined if a route or its ancestors are not yet registered during startup and automatically updates once finalized.

sites.last_line: Fixed route resolution during app bootstrap. `RouteResolver` now returns `undefined` instead of throwing a `No path for ...` error when an ancestor route ref has not yet been registered, which can happen at startup while only a partial extension tree is instantiated. `RouteResolutionApiProxy` now also supports `subscribe` and notifies its subscribers when route resolution is re-initialized at app finalization, so that route refs that could not be resolved earlier are resolved again.

sites.last_line: Added an optional `subscribe` method to `RouteResolutionApi`, which notifies listeners when the route resolution state changes. The `useRouteRef` hook now uses it to re-resolve routes when the route resolution state is updated after the app has been finalized, so that route refs that could not be resolved during bootstrap no longer remain `undefined`.
